title: Photonic CZ gates based on few-photon scattering from emitter-cavity systems
abstract: In this paper we analyze the performance of photonic CZ gates based on N waveguide-coupled cavities containing two-level emitters. We derive single- and two-photon scattering matrices for one cavity using the input-output formalism of quantum optics and for N>1 cavities using the SLH formalism, allowing us to compute the CZ gate fidelity. We consider two input Gaussian wave packets that are centered on a two-photon transition of the emitter-cavity system, and find a trade-off between optimizing the single-photon and two-photon wave packet shape. While the single-photon wave packet is preserved for large emitter-cavity coupling rates, where there is little overlap with the single-photon transitions, the two-photon wave packet acquires the necessary $π$ phase shift for smaller coupling rates, comparable to the cavity decay rate multiplied by the number of cavities. We find that this trade-off limits the CZ gate fidelity to approximately 60% when averaging over all input states.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the performance of photonic CZ gates realized through two-photon scattering from arrays of coupled emitter-cavity systems. By deriving scattering matrices using advanced quantum optics formalisms, the authors quantify the gate fidelity. They conclude that optimizing the required two-photon interaction leads to a fundamental trade-off, limiting the average gate fidelity to about 60%.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing a deterministic two-photon Controlled-Z (CZ) gate in photonic quantum computing, which requires non-linear photon-photon interactions.
main_result: The trade-off between optimizing the single-photon and two-photon wave packet shapes limits the average CZ gate fidelity to approximately 60% when averaged over all input states.
method: The authors derive single- and two-photon scattering matrices using the input-output formalism for single cavities and the SLH formalism for multiple coupled cavities.
model_or_system: The system utilizes photonic CZ gates based on few-photon scattering from N waveguide-coupled cavities containing two-level emitters, analogous to the KLM scheme.
key_observables: CZ gate fidelity ($F_{CZ}$) and average CZ gate fidelity ($ ar{F}_{CZ}$).
important_parameters: Coupling rates, cavity decay rates ($\Gamma$), and the number of cavities ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a simple passive emitter-cavity system without active control over emitter or cavity parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the CZ gate in the KLM scheme and its proposed implementation using N waveguide-coupled cavities, detailing coupling rates and decay parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical setup and the required gate operation. It then derives the necessary scattering matrices using quantum optics formalisms (input-output and SLH) to calculate the gate fidelity based on input wave packet optimization.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles a core physical challenge in quantum computing—generating controlled non-linear interactions using solid-state emitters—providing quantitative fidelity estimates for a promising platform.
